comparisons.peer_summary: Sales are primarily made via purchase orders or agreements, but these do not necessarily indicate future sales as they may be revised or canceled without penalty.
comparisons.comparison: Both QCOM and AMD disclose that their sales are primarily conducted via purchase orders, but highlight the resulting uncertainty and risk. QCOM focuses on the operational flexibility this provides to customers, stating they 'generally allows customers to reschedule delivery dates... and to cancel orders prior to shipment.' In contrast, AMD emphasizes the financial risk and lack of certainty for the seller, noting that these orders 'may not necessarily be indicative of actual sales... as some of these orders or agreements may be revised or canceled without penalty.' While both acknowledge the cancellation/revision mechanism, QCOM frames it as a service feature, whereas AMD frames it as a revenue visibility risk.

sentences.text: QCT generally allows customers to reschedule delivery dates within a defined time frame and to cancel orders prior to shipment with or without payment of a cancellation fee, depending on when the order is canceled.
QCT's sales are primarily made through supply terms which implement a purchase order and order confirmation process for delivery of products.
Sales are made primarily pursuant to purchase orders for current delivery or agreements covering purchases over a period of time.

Although such orders or agreements may provide visibility into future quarters, they may not necessarily be indicative of actual sales for any succeeding period as some of these orders or agreements may be revised or canceled without penalty.

comparisons.peer_summary: AMD markets products through direct and co-marketing programs, including cooperative advertising with customers and third parties where market development funds may be provided for eligible customers to reimburse for advertisements related to AMD and third-party systems.
comparisons.comparison: Both QCOM and AMD utilize similar marketing structures involving direct efforts and partner collaborations. QCOM states that products are marketed 'Through direct marketing efforts, partnerships and collaborations (including marketing programs with customers)' to promote brand awareness. AMD similarly describes marketing its products 'through direct marketing and co-marketing programs' and having 'cooperative advertising and marketing programs with customers and third parties.' Both companies leverage these collaborative programs to expand brand reach and support customer adoption, though QCOM specifically links this to the 'Snapdragon' brand premium positioning while AMD details the provision of funds and materials.

sentences.text: Through direct marketing efforts, partnerships and collaborations (including marketing programs with customers), products powered by Snapdragon and Qualcomm technologies are marketed to expand the reach of both brands to drive awareness and preference.

QCT's marketing strategy aims to promote Qualcomm as the leader of enabling intelligent computing everywhere, and Snapdragon as the preferred platform brand powering premium experiences across handsets, automotive and IoT.
We market our products through direct marketing and co-marketing programs.

In addition, we have cooperative advertising and marketing programs with customers and third parties, including market development programs, pursuant to which we may provide product information, training, marketing materials and funds.

comparisons.peer_summary: Broadcom sells products via direct sales force, distributors, and channel partners, with distributors and OEMs/contract manufacturers accounting for the substantial majority of semiconductor sales. The company utilizes a mix of large global distributors, regional distributors, and direct relationships with OEMs, supported by specialized sales forces and logistics infrastructure.
comparisons.comparison: Both QCOM and AVGO rely on direct sales forces supported by channel partners, but differ in channel composition and emphasis. QCOM describes sales made through 'supply terms which implement a purchase order and order confirmation process,' implying a direct ordering relationship with customers. AVGO explicitly structures its channel as a 'direct sales force and a select network of distributors and channel partners,' noting that 'Distributors and OEMs, or their contract manufacturers, typically account for the substantial majority of our semiconductor sales.' While QCOM focuses on the transactional mechanism (purchase orders), AVGO focuses on the distribution infrastructure (distributors/OEMs) and the specialized role of its direct sales force in supporting large OEMs.

sentences.text: QCT's sales are primarily made through supply terms which implement a purchase order and order confirmation process for delivery of products.

QCT generally allows customers to reschedule delivery dates within a defined time frame and to cancel orders prior to shipment with or without payment of a cancellation fee, depending on when the order is canceled.
We sell our products through our direct sales force and a select network of distributors and channel partners globally.
Distributors and OEMs, or their contract manufacturers, typically account for the substantial majority of our semiconductor sales.

Our direct sales force focuses on supporting our large OEM customers, and has specialized product and service knowledge that enables us to sell specific offerings at key levels throughout a customer's organization.

peer_results.rationale: While INTC mentions cooperative advertising, its primary disclosures in the provided candidates focus on IP protection, trademark usage, and R&D investment strategies. There is no candidate comparable to QCOM's specific disclosure on sales order mechanics (purchase orders/cancellations) or its specific marketing strategy focused on promoting the Snapdragon/Qualcomm brands through direct and partner efforts in the same manner. The INTC disclosures are thematically distinct (IP/R&D vs. Sales Channel/Marketing Execution).

comparisons.peer_summary: Semiconductor products are marketed primarily through a direct sales force, distributors, retailers, and independent representatives, with Crucial-branded products also sold via web-based direct sales. Inventory is maintained near key customers for rapid delivery, and distributors typically stock competitors' products as well.
comparisons.comparison: Both QCOM and MU utilize direct sales forces and distributors, but MU explicitly includes independent representatives and a direct-to-consumer web channel for its Crucial brand. QCOM describes a process centered on 'purchase order and order confirmation' with flexibility for rescheduling/cancellation, without mentioning independent reps or web sales in this specific disclosure. MU states it markets 'primarily through our own direct sales force' and also through 'distributors, retailers, and independent sales representatives,' alongside 'web-based direct sales channel' for Crucial. Both highlight the mix of direct and channel sales, but MU provides more granularity on the types of intermediaries (retailers, independent reps) and direct consumer access.

QCT's marketing strategy aims to promote Qualcomm as the leader of enabling intelligent computing everywhere, and Snapdragon as the preferred platform brand powering premium experiences across handsets, automotive and IoT.
We market our semiconductor memory and storage products primarily through our own direct sales force and maintain sales or representative offices to support our worldwide customer base.
Our products are also offered through distributors, retailers, and independent sales representatives.
We sell our Crucial-branded products through a web-based customer-direct sales channel as well as through channel and distribution partners.

comparisons.peer_topic: Global Sales and Partner Network Strategy
comparisons.peer_summary: The company's sales and marketing strategy aims to provide high-performance computing platforms and software through a global network of partners including CSPs, OEMs, and ISVs.
comparisons.comparison: Both QCOM and NVDA explicitly highlight the strategic importance of partnerships and ecosystems in their marketing and sales strategies. QCOM states that products are marketed through 'partnerships and collaborations (including marketing programs with customers)' to drive awareness. NVDA describes its strategy as working 'closely with end customers and various industry ecosystems through our partner network,' which incorporates a wide array of partners including CSPs, OEMs, and ISVs. Both companies view partner ecosystems as integral to their brand promotion and market reach, though NVDA provides a more detailed taxonomy of its partner types.

sentences.text: Through direct marketing efforts, partnerships and collaborations (including marketing programs with customers), products powered by Snapdragon and Qualcomm technologies are marketed to expand the reach of both brands to drive awareness and preference.

QCT's marketing strategy aims to promote Qualcomm as the leader of enabling intelligent computing everywhere, and Snapdragon as the preferred platform brand powering premium experiences across handsets, automotive and IoT.
Our sales and marketing teams, located across our global markets, work closely with end customers and various industry ecosystems through our partner network.

Our partner network incorporates global, regional and specialized CSPs, OEMs, ODMs, system integrators, independent software vendors, or ISVs, add-in board manufacturers, or AIBs, distributors, automotive manufacturers and tier-1 automotive suppliers, and other ecosystem participants.
